run.question:
We have an active P1 incident — the checkout service in our production-us-east-2
cluster is throwing 500 errors and customers cannot complete payments. Please
investigate the root cause using the app-260-prod-logs index.

report.summary: The failure evidence exists only in the Elasticsearch index app-260-prod-logs, and all of it is dated 2026-11-21 between 02:45:22Z and 05:40:22Z. Eight of the ten documents are labeled cluster=production-us-east-2; two INFO rows are labeled cluster=production-eu-west-2 and report a healthy checkout (p95 230ms) and normal Stripe-EU. In production-us-east-2 the checkout-service logged four 500s (03:45:22Z, 04:45:22Z, 05:15:22Z, 05:40:22Z) whose own messages name the payment path as the failure point: payment-provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us), payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway, and circuit-breaker open for payment-service at a 41% failure rate. The payment-service in the same cluster logged 504s saying 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 03:45:22Z and 05:00:22Z, and at 05:30:22Z warned that Stripe-US degraded mode was acknowledged via status page with a retry queue depth of 1031. Read together, the checkout 500s trace to timeouts/failures in its payment dependency, and payment-service's own dependency stripe-us is where the fault originates; why stripe-us was degraded is not observable from this data. Kubernetes data was only readable for a cluster whose otel-demo checkout and payment pods processed payments successfully throughout 05:17-05:45Z, so it is not the failing production-us-east-2 workload and nothing in it is named as this incident's root cause. Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on every attempt, so error-rate and latency signals and traces are unknown, and no latency trend is claimed from the single 02:45:22Z p95=1700ms warning.

claims.text: The only Elasticsearch index that exists is app-260-prod-logs (green, 10 documents). Its mapping contains timestamp (date), cluster, region, service, level, status_code, correlation_id and message, so the log data carries its own cluster/region identity.

All 10 documents in app-260-prod-logs were returned, covering 2026-11-21T02:45:22Z to 2026-11-21T05:40:22Z. Eight are labeled cluster=production-us-east-2; two INFO rows are labeled cluster=production-eu-west-2.

checkout-service in production-us-east-2 logged four ERROR/500 events: at 03:45:22Z 'POST /api/checkout failed: payment provider response timeout after 30s (provider=stripe-us)' (correlation_id chk-us-2142); at 04:45:22Z 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service (failure rate 41% > 25% threshold)'; at 05:15:22Z 'payment provider returned 502 Bad Gateway' (chk-us-2252); and at 05:40:22Z 'circuit-breaker open for payment-service' (chk-us-2280).

payment-service in production-us-east-2 logged ERROR 504 'Upstream timeout calling stripe-us /v1/charges after 30000ms' at 03:45:22Z (chk-us-2142) and at 05:00:22Z (chk-us-2220), and a WARN at 05:30:22Z stating 'Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page; retry queue depth=1031'.

The earliest production-us-east-2 row is a checkout-service WARN at 02:45:22Z with status 200: 'Latency on POST /api/checkout p95=1700ms (target 800ms)'. This is one reported reading; no baseline series was available to establish a trend.

The two production-eu-west-2 rows describe a healthy cluster, not this incident: checkout-service INFO at 03:45:22Z 'Healthy: p95 latency 230ms over last 5 minutes' and payment-service INFO at 04:45:22Z 'Stripe-EU responding normally, p95 latency 180ms'.

In the only Kubernetes cluster I could read (namespace otel-demo), the checkout pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n logged 'payment went through' for repeated orders between 05:26:33Z and 05:45:12Z, and the payment pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d logged 'Transaction complete' requests between 05:17:32Z and 05:45:12Z. This workload was succeeding, so it is not the failing production-us-east-2 checkout.

In that same otel-demo cluster both the checkout container (checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n) and the payment container (payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d) have lastState terminated with exitCode 255, reason Unknown, finishedAt 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z, and both restarted at 2026-11-21T04:23:48Z (restartCount 1). No earlier container log stream was available for either pod.

The otel-demo ConfigMap flagd-config declares fault-injection flags 'paymentFailure' (variants 100%/90%/75%/50%/25%/10%/off, defaultVariant 'off') and 'paymentUnreachable' (on/off, defaultVariant 'off'), and the checkout deployment resolves PAYMENT_ADDR=payment:8080 with FLAGD_HOST=flagd / FLAGD_PORT=8013.

The readable Kubernetes objects carry no cluster or region name: the single node is opspilot-m1-control-plane with no topology.kubernetes.io/region label, and deployments exist in namespaces app-100a, kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo. No Kubernetes object in that cluster can be tied by its own labels to production-us-east-2.

Events in the readable cluster between 05:28:04Z and 05:43:04Z are Normal rollout events for app-100a workloads (Deployment 'loki' and 'payment-api-100a' ScalingReplicaSet from 0 to 1, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started) plus one Warning Endpoints FailedToCreateEndpoint at 05:28:04Z ('Failed to create endpoint for service app-282/loki: endpoints "loki" already exists'). None of these events name the checkout or payment workloads or the production-us-east-2 cluster.

The checkout 500s in production-us-east-2 are caused downstream by stripe-us: payment-service's call to stripe-us /v1/charges times out at 30s (504), stripe-us also returns 502 through the payment path, and checkout's payment circuit breaker then opens at a 41% failure rate and returns 500. The logs show the mechanism at payment-service and at checkout but not why stripe-us itself degraded.

An alternative to stripe-us being slow is a degraded network/egress path between payment-service and stripe-us in production-us-east-2: the logged symptom is a 30s timeout and a 502, which does not by itself distinguish provider-side slowness from a network path problem. No metric or trace data was available to separate these.

The Kubernetes workloads I could read were healthy for this payment path: their checkout and payment containers logged successful charge completions throughout 05:17-05:45Z, so those pods cannot be named as affected by the production-us-east-2 payment failures.

The flagd fault-injection settings that could break payments are declared off (paymentFailure defaultVariant 'off', paymentUnreachable defaultVariant 'off') in the only ConfigMap I could read, and the pods that consume that flagd were completing payments successfully in the same window, so those settings are not evidence of a fault in effect in that cluster.

Considered and rejected as the cause of the production-us-east-2 checkout 500s: the 04:23:42Z exitCode 255 termination and 04:23:48Z restart of the otel-demo checkout and payment containers. Those containers are in the readable cluster, which completed payments successfully after the restart, while the production-us-east-2 errors continued to 05:40:22Z in the log index.

Considered and rejected for this incident: the flagd paymentFailure / paymentUnreachable flags as the trigger of the checkout 500s. The declared defaults in flagd-config are 'off', the flagd-consuming checkout and payment pods in that cluster logged successful transactions throughout the window, and that cluster is not the cluster where the 500s were logged.

gaps: No Prometheus data: every attempt (execute_prometheus_instant_query at 2026-11-21T05:40:00Z, metrics_range_query on 04:45:33Z-05:45:33Z, get_all_labels, get_metric_names) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so error-rate, latency and request-volume series for checkout-service and payment-service are unknown, and no baseline exists for the 02:45:22Z p95=1700ms warning.
No Jaeger data: traces_search and traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so span-level error status and the checkout -> payment -> stripe call graph are unknown.

No Kubernetes objects for production-us-east-2: the readable cluster is a different one (otel-demo/app-100a workloads, single node opspilot-m1-control-plane, no region label), so the production-us-east-2 checkout/payment pods, their restarts, events, ConfigMaps and deployment history could not be inspected, and no ConfigMap or other setting in production-us-east-2 was checked for fault-injection fields.
What caused stripe-us to degrade (30s timeouts and 502 responses) is not observable here; only one status-page acknowledgement line in payment-service's log refers to it.
Change history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so configuration or deployment changes in production-us-east-2 before or during 02:45-05:40Z could not be checked.

Payment-provider endpoint and credential configuration for production-us-east-2 was not readable (no Kubernetes access to that cluster, and Secrets cannot be read), so a misconfigured stripe-us endpoint cannot be ruled in or out.

The exitCode 255 / reason Unknown termination of the otel-demo checkout and payment containers at 2026-11-21T04:23:42Z has no readable cause: previous container logs were empty and no events for those pods were retained; it is recorded as an unexplained change in that cluster, not as impact of this incident.
next_steps: Confirm with the payment provider's status/incident feed whether stripe-us had a degradation covering 2026-11-21T02:45Z-05:40Z, matching the 'Stripe-US degraded mode acknowledged via status page' log line.

From a target with access to production-us-east-2, check payment-service egress (DNS resolution, connection establishment, TLS latency to the stripe-us endpoint) to separate provider degradation from a network-path problem.

From a target with access to production-us-east-2, read the checkout and payment Deployments and their ConfigMaps/feature flags for any enabled payment failure/timeout/latency injection or an incorrect payment-provider endpoint, and check pod restart/OOM events during 02:45-05:40Z.
Restore or provide Prometheus and Jaeger access so checkout-service and payment-service error rates and the payment client span latency can be established against a pre-incident baseline.
